# Purpose

This file imports raw data provided by Alison Masyr and Caitlin Eliason that 
contains observations of dogs receiving CHOP chemotherapy at MSU Veterinary 
Medicine Clinic (VMC) between 2016 and 2022. This file does some data cleaning 
and management, then saves out revised data files that will be used for the 
analyses in other scripts. 

::: {.callout-note}
The data file we received was called `Vinc Cases 1.9.23.xlsx`, but we renamed it 
to `Vinc Cases 1.9.24.xlsx` before using it because that was the date we 
received it. 
:::

# Setup

This section documents some setup tasks that are useful to the statistician on 
the team. Most readers of this document will probably want skip directly to 
@sec-Data-Mgt.

## Define Global Options

Global R chunk options are defined in the YAML header but local chunk options
will over-ride global options. We can temporarily disable an individual chunk by
inserting `#| eval: false` on a line at the top of the chunk.

## Load Packages

Load R packages that we need to get additional functions.

```{r}
#| label: load-packages
library(here)       # for here(), i_am()
library(dplyr)      # for filter(), group_by(), mutate(), rename(), summarise()
library(knitr)      # for kable()
library(kableExtra) # for kable_styling 
library(gtsummary)  # for 
library(readxl)     # for read_xlsx()
library(quarto)     # for quarto_version()
library(CHOPStudy)  # for version info 
```

## Declare Path

```{r}
#| label: declare-path

here::i_am(path = "scripts/Import_Data.qmd")
```

## Read Data {#sec-Read-Data}

```{r}
#| label: import-data

Raw_CHOP <- read_xlsx(here("../Data/Vinc Cases 1.9.24.xlsx")) 
names(Raw_CHOP)
```

# Data Management {#sec-Data-Mgt}
The first task is just renaming variables. After that, we also need to convert 
some to factors and compute some additional variables. 

The units of measurement for `Total_Bands` are 1000/ul and some are not integers 
(they have non-zero digits to the right of the decimal place). Therefore, we 
rescaled into a new variable that has units of 100/ul by computing 
`Total_Bands_Rescale = Total_Bands*10`. That rescaled variable was used in  
count models because those require non-negative integer values for all counts. 
We also created log transformed versions of both `Total_Bands` and 
`Total_Bands_Rescaled` for use in graphing data. Because `log(0) = -Infinity`, 
we recode the `-Infinity` values for `log_Total_Bands` to -5 and the `-Infinity` 
values for `log_Total_Bands_Rescaled` to -3 so that we can make compact graphs 
of the distributions. 

```{r}
#| label: create-All_CHOP

All_CHOP <- Raw_CHOP %>% 
  rename(Patient = `Patient Number`,
         Visit_Number = `Visit #`,
         CHOP_Start_Date = `CHOP start date`,
         Phase_of_Treatment = `Phase of treatment`,
         CHOP_Number = `CHOP number`,
         CBC_Date = `CBC date`,
         Total_WBC = `Total WBC (x10.e3/uL)`,
         Total_Neutrophil = `Total neutrophil`,
         Total_Bands = `Total bands`, 
         Bandemia_Grade = `Bandemia grade`,
         Weight_kg = kg,
         Surface_Area_m2 = `m^2`,
         Notes = `...15`) %>% 
  mutate(Patient = factor(Patient),
         Days_Since_Start = as.numeric(CBC_Date - CHOP_Start_Date, units = "days"),
         Weeks = Days_Since_Start/7,
         Total_Bands_Rescaled = Total_Bands*10,
         log_Total_Bands = if_else(Total_Bands == 0, 
                                   true = -5, 
                                   false = log(Total_Bands)),
         log_Total_Bands_Rescaled = if_else(Total_Bands_Rescaled == 0, 
                                   true = -3, 
                                   false = log(Total_Bands_Rescaled)),
         Bandemia = if_else(Total_Bands >= 0.2, true = 1, false = 0)) %>% 
  arrange(Patient, CHOP_Number, Visit_Number, CBC_Date)

# Show the updated variable names to confirm all looks right. 
names(All_CHOP)
```

::: {.callout-note}
In previous versions of the output (2024-04-02 and earlier), we had been 
recoding Patient_Number values > 28 by subtracting 1 from them just to make the 
whole sent of numbers sequential. We removed that code because it makes no 
functional difference to our analyses and it is easier to cross-reference back 
to source data file if we don't do that. 
:::

## Fix Negative Values for Weeks Since CHOP Started
Here, we examine when a CBC lab sample was collected via the `Weeks` variable, 
which measures how many weeks had elapsed between the start of the CHOP protocol 
and collection of the CBC sample. This should always be a positive number, so 
any negative values are implausible and should be corrected if possible. 

@tbl-negative-weeks shows that there are two patients with `Weeks < 0`. The 
`CBC_Date` values are clearly implausible. Therefore we will examine data for 
those two patients more closely in @tbl-patient55 and @tbl-patient80. 

```{r}
#| label: tbl-negative-weeks
#| tbl-cap: Records with Implausible Visit Timing (Weeks < 0)

All_CHOP %>% 
  filter(Weeks < 0) %>% 
  select(Patient, MRN, Visit_Number, CHOP_Start_Date, CBC_Date, Weeks) %>% 
  kable(digits = 2) %>% 
  kable_styling()
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-patient55
#| tbl-cap: Visit Dates for Patient 55 (Before Corrections)

All_CHOP %>% 
  filter(Patient == 55) %>%
  select(Patient, CHOP_Number, Visit_Number, CHOP_Start_Date, CBC_Date, Weeks) %>% 
  kable(digits = 2) %>%
  kable_styling()
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-patient80
#| tbl-cap: Visit Dates for Patient 80 (Before Corrections)

All_CHOP %>% 
  filter(Patient == 80) %>%
  select(Patient, CHOP_Number, Visit_Number, CHOP_Start_Date, CBC_Date, Weeks) %>% 
  kable(digits = 2) %>%
  kable_styling()
```

::: {.callout-caution}
Both patients 55 (@@tbl-patient55) and 80 (@@tbl-patient80) each have one visit 
with a clearly inaccurate date where the year was entered as 1930 instead of 
2020. For both dates, correcting the year while leaving the month and day 
portions of the date alone will correct the error and yield dates that make 
sense given the sequence and temporal spacing of other visits for that patient. 
:::

Below we fix the `CBC_Date` and then re-calculate variables that depended on it. 

```{r}
#| label: fix-patient55_80
All_CHOP <- All_CHOP %>% 
  mutate(CBC_Date = case_when(Patient == 55 & CBC_Date == as.POSIXct("1930-08-03", tz = "UTC") 
                              ~ as.POSIXct("2020-08-03", tz = "UTC"), 
                              Patient == 80 & CBC_Date == as.POSIXct("1930-01-30", tz = "UTC") 
                              ~ as.POSIXct("2020-01-30", tz = "UTC"),
                              .default = CBC_Date),
         # Re-compute variables that depend on CBC_Date. 
         Days_Since_Start = as.numeric(CBC_Date - CHOP_Start_Date, units = "days"),
         Weeks = Days_Since_Start/7)
```

## Fix Extreme Positive Values for Weeks Since CHOP Started
We've fixed negative values for `Weeks`, but still need to look for any other 
outlier values that may be data quality problems. So, we look at a summary by
visit number. We're looking for aggregate statistics that don't make sense and 
could be caused by data entry errors in the `CBC_Date` variable. 
@tbl-Visit-Timing1 shows descriptive statistics for the visit timing broken down 
by visit number. 

```{r}
#| label: tbl-Visit-Timing1 
#| tbl-cap: Descriptive Statistics for Visit Timing (Weeks Since CHOP Started)

All_CHOP %>% 
  group_by(Visit_Number) %>% 
  summarise(mean_weeks = mean(Weeks, na.rm = TRUE),
            sd_weeks = sd(Weeks, na.rm = TRUE),
            min_weeks = min(Weeks, na.rm = TRUE),
            max_weeks = max(Weeks, na.rm = TRUE)) %>% 
  kable(digits = 2) %>% 
  kable_styling()
```

:::{.callout-caution}
Note: The mean, SD, and maximum number of weeks since CHOP started are all 
unexpectedly large at visit 3 and don't make sense given the expected timing of 
events under the CHOP protocol. That implies a data problem we need to 
investigate and fix. 
:::

@tbl-outlier-weeks shows the records for patient visits where `Weeks > 34`, 
which was just a bit higher than the the maximum number of weeks seen at any 
other visit number. We can see that Patient = 62 is a very clear outlier, with a 
`CBC_Date` in the future. That's clearly a data entry error. So, now we inspect 
data for `Patient = 62` more closely to determine if we can fix the anomalous 
date. @tbl-patient62 shows all the records for that patient. 

```{r}
#| label: tbl-outlier-weeks
#| tbl-cap: Visit 3 Records with Implausible Visit Timing (Weeks > 34)

All_CHOP %>% 
  filter(Visit_Number == 3 & Weeks > 34) %>% 
  select(Patient, MRN, Visit_Number, CHOP_Start_Date, CBC_Date, Weeks) %>% 
  kable(digits = 2) %>% 
  kable_styling()
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-patient62
#| tbl-cap: Visit Dates for Patient 62 (Before Corrections)

All_CHOP %>% 
  filter(Patient == 62) %>%
  select(Patient, CHOP_Number, Visit_Number, CHOP_Start_Date, CBC_Date, Weeks) %>% 
  kable(digits = 2) %>%
  kable_styling()
```

::: {.callout-caution}
It is clear that for `Patient = 62`, visit 3 should have occurred in the year
2018 instead of 2028. We assume the month and day are accurate because after
correcting the year, the `CBC_Date` for visit 3 would fall between those for
visits 2 and 4. The sequence would then be sensible.
:::

Below we fix the `CBC_Date` and then re-calculate variables that depended on it. 

```{r}
#| label: fix-patient62
All_CHOP <- All_CHOP %>% 
  mutate(CBC_Date = if_else(Patient == 62 & CBC_Date == as.POSIXct("2028-05-25", 
                                                                   tz = "UTC"), 
                            true =  as.POSIXct("2018-05-25", tz = "UTC"), 
                            false = CBC_Date),
         # Re-compute variables that depend on CBC_Date. 
         Days_Since_Start = as.numeric(CBC_Date - CHOP_Start_Date, units = "days"),
         Weeks = Days_Since_Start/7)
```

## Recheck for Outlier Values for Weeks Since CHOP Started
We've fixed negative values for Weeks, but still need to look for any other 
outlier values that may be data quality problems. So, we look at a summary by
visit number. We're looking for aggregate statistics that don't make sense and 
could be caused by data entry errors in the `CBC_Date` variable. 
@tbl-Visit-Timing2 shows descriptive statistics for the visit timing broken down 
by visit number. 

```{r}
#| label: tbl-Visit-Timing2 
#| tbl-cap: Updated Descriptive Statistics for Visit Timing (Weeks Since CHOP Started)

All_CHOP %>% 
  group_by(Visit_Number) %>% 
  summarise(mean_weeks = mean(Weeks, na.rm = TRUE),
            sd_weeks = sd(Weeks, na.rm = TRUE),
            min_weeks = min(Weeks, na.rm = TRUE),
            max_weeks = max(Weeks, na.rm = TRUE)) %>% 
  kable(digits = 2) %>% 
  kable_styling()
```

:::{.callout-tip}
Note: The descriptive statistics now look much more sensible. 
:::

@fig-visualize_weeks is a boxplot that visualize the information of weeks.

```{r}
#| label: fig-visualize_weeks
#| fig-cap: Time since first visit in weeks per visit
boxplot(Weeks ~ Visit_Number, data = All_CHOP, xlab="Visit Number")
```

## Create More Variables
After reading peer review feedback on a manuscript that got rejected, the team 
decided on 2024-08-29 to narrow the focus of the analyses. We will now focus 
only on data for patients who had their first visit within 2 weeks of 
their CHOP start date. This section creates variables we can use to implement 
that decision

First we create a subset of the data containing only records for visit 1 within 
the respective CHOP cycles, then add a logical variable marking which visit 1 
observations had `CBC_Dates` indicating that the lab sample was collected within 
2 weeks of the start of that CHOP cycle. 

``` {r}
#| label: create-Visit1_CHOP

Visit1_CHOP <- All_CHOP %>% 
  filter(Visit_Number == 1) %>% 
  mutate(Started_in_2Weeks = Weeks <= 2) %>% 
  select(Patient, CHOP_Number, Started_in_2Weeks)
```

Next we merge that new `Started_in_2Weeks` variable back onto the full dataset. 
We can then use it later to select cases. 

``` {r}
#| label: merge-All_CHOP-Visit1_CHOP

All_CHOP <- left_join(x = All_CHOP, y = Visit1_CHOP, 
                      by = join_by(Patient, CHOP_Number)) 
```

## Summarize Amount of Data
The first thing to do is summarize how much data there is before we start 
applying any selection criteria. 

```{r}
#| label: tbl-amt-data
#| tbl-cap: Amount of Raw Data

Step1 <- All_CHOP %>% 
  count(Patient) %>% 
  summarise(Step = 1,
            Event = "All raw data", 
            N_Dogs = n(),
            N_Observations = sum(n))

Step1 %>% 
  kable() %>% 
  kable_styling()
```

## Subset the Data 
Here, we select a subset of records that we want to use for the study, namely 
we retain only records for the first phase of the first instance of using the 
CHOP protocol (`CHOP_Number` = 1) for each patient. We retain only data about 
drug 1 (vincristine), drug 2 (cyclophosphamide), and drug 3 (doxorubicin). The drug
selection is motivated by the fact that we don't have enough data about other
drugs.

```{r}
#| label: create-Subset_CHOP
#| execute: false

Final_CHOP <- All_CHOP %>% 
  mutate(Drop_Step = case_when(CHOP_Number >= 2 ~ 1, 
                               Phase_of_Treatment != 1 ~ 2,
                               !Drug %in% 1:3 ~ 3)
```


# Save Data

``` {r}
#| label: create-save-what

# Character vector of object names that will be saved.
save_what <- c("Raw_CHOP", "All_CHOP", "Subset_CHOP")
```

``` {r}
#| label: save-data

save(list = save_what, 
     file=here("data/Imported_CHOP_Data.RData"))
```

::: {.callout-tip}
The current data file can be loaded into R by copying the following code chunk 
into a script, setting the chunk option `eval: true`, and running the chunk. 
That will overwrite any objects already in memory that have the same names as 
the objects being loaded.

``` {r}
#| label: load-data
#| eval: false

load(file=here("data/Imported_CHOP_Data.RData"))
```
:::

# Software Information
This section documents information that is important for reproducibility. Most
users will not need to read it. It is primarily here for use by the statistician
on the team.

We used [R](https://www.r-project.org/) as our main computing environment and
[Quarto](https://quarto.org/) scripts to enhance reproducibility. We used
[RStudio](www.rstudio.org) as the editor to interface with R and Quarto.

- Software chain:
  **qmd file > RStudio > Quarto > R > knitr > md file > Pandoc > HTML file**.
- Source file: **`r params$SourceFile`**
- Output file: **`r params$LogFile`**
- [Quarto `r quarto_version()`](https://quarto.org/) runs `*.qmd` files through 
  [R](https://www.r-project.org/) and [knitr](https://yihui.org/knitr/) to 
  produce `*.md` markdown files.
- [Pandoc `r rmarkdown::pandoc_version()`](https://pandoc.org) converts markdown 
  files (`*.md`) to other formats, including LaTeX (`*.tex`) and HTML (`*.html`) 
  among others.
